raw_response:
I farm only these 10.1 mu, so I cannot play around too much. Same as most years, I will keep the wheat-maize rotation on all the land. Wheat and maize together are the safest for me. If one side is poor, the other can still help. I do not read those technical papers, I look at my own field and what people around me do. Last year the wheat did all right when I gave enough base fertilizer and watered at the important times, so this year I will do about the same. Fertilizer is expensive, but if I cut too much and the crop turns yellow, then the loss is bigger than the saving. Still, I cannot spend wildly because the family needs cash and some people are away working.

For wheat, I will sow in early October after the maize is cleared, using a common local improved seed that people nearby buy from the dealer. I will put most fertilizer before sowing, then give another small topdress when the wheat starts standing up strong in spring. With the well, I will water a few times if the season is dry, especially before winter, at jointing, and around grain filling. After wheat harvest in June, I will rush to plant summer maize on the same land right away. That window is short, so I will keep tillage simple and use the same practical way as usual. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, put fertilizer at planting and then one more time when it is growing fast. If rain is decent, I may only irrigate once or twice, but if it stays dry I will use the well because maize without water in summer can lose badly.
